text: Saint James Power Station: The Coal-Fired Station of 1926

The red-brick building at HarbourFront began as a coal-fired power station — Singapore's first municipal power station — and its first generator was commissioned a century ago, on the 30th of September 1926.
Singapore needed a proper power station, built for the town rather than borrowed from the docks and the trams.
The first unit, the 2,000 kilowatt generator, was installed and commissioned on the 30th of September 1926, running only from 6 to 11 in the evening to shave the peak.

The Commissioners, foreseeing still more demand, authorised an additional 10,000 kilowatt set that June, bringing the plant to about 22,000 kilowatts — almost seven times the roughly 3,200 kilowatts of everything that had come before.

Singapore's coal initially arrived from Manchuria, shipped through Japanese firms that were the lowest tenderers, until that supply stopped in the late 1930s; after that, coal came from Peninsular Malaysia.
So the famous coal-fired station burned coal for only about fourteen of its fifty years.
There were blackouts as early as 1928, and one shutdown that November was traced to the negligence of junior shift engineers, who were dismissed.

When the expatriate engineers were interned in Changi, local staff kept the station and the distribution network running under the Japanese — two Japanese supervisors over the distribution section, and Singaporean foremen and assistants below them, improvising spare parts off the black market.
The two tall chimneys that define the building today date from this rebuild; the west chimney, 32 metres high, now houses the station's heritage gallery.
The last of its gas turbines was decommissioned in 1976 — fifty years after the first small generator had been switched on to cover the evening peak.
Keeping the name Saint James Power Station, the complex officially launched on the 24th of September 2006 with 12 outlets for live entertainment, music and dining, holding more than 10,000 people.

On the 11th of November 2009 the National Heritage Board gazetted Saint James Power Station a national monument — the 60th building or site so gazetted — while the nightclubs were still trading inside it.
A century after its first generator was commissioned, the coal station is a technology company's world headquarters, and its chimney carries the word "dyson".
